In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type $\frac{\infty }{\infty },$ so applying L'Hopital's rule yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{3/2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[{x}^{3/2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x]^{′}}{[{x}^{2}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\frac{3}{2}{x}^{1/2}+\frac{1}{x}}{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{3/2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{1/2}+\frac{1}{x}]}^{′}}{[2x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\frac{3}{4}{x}^{-1/2}-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}}{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
